instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to shoulder height and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your right hand, palm down, arm bent 90 degrees and held in front of you parallel to the floor.
3. Drive your elbow out to the side while straightening your arm, pulling the cable across your body.
4. Squeeze your rear shoulder and upper back at the end of the movement.
5. Return your arm to the start under control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and keep the upper arm moving back, not just the hand.
2. Keep the torso still and avoid using momentum.
3. Exhale as you drive the arm out, inhale as you return.
4. Keep the wrist neutral throughout.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to shoulder height and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your right hand, palm down, arm bent 90 degrees and held in front of you parallel to the floor.
3. Keep the elbow bent at 90 degrees and drive it out to the side, pulling the cable across your body.
4. Squeeze your rear shoulder and shoulder blades at the end of the movement.
5. Return your arm to the start under control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow fixed at 90 degrees so the rear delt does the work.
2. Pull the shoulder blade back rather than just moving the arm.
3. Keep the torso still and avoid swinging.
4. Exhale as you drive out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley and sit with your knees secured under the pads, feet flat.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and extend your arms overhead.
3. Keep your back straight and pull the bar down behind your neck by driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your back at the bottom of the movement.
5. Extend your arms back overhead under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light load and avoid forcing the bar low behind the neck to protect the shoulders.
2. Drive the movement with the elbows, not the hands.
3. Keep the core tight and avoid leaning or using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you extend up.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, palms down, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended down.
3. Keep your upper arms still against your sides and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze the forearms at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrists firm and straight throughout.
2. Keep the elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging.
3. Use a lighter load than a standard curl since the grip is weaker.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to shoulder height on a cable crossover and stand in the center.
2. Grasp the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand so the cables cross in front of you.
3. Stand with a slight bend in your elbows and arms extended in front at shoulder height.
4. Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc until they are level with your shoulders.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows and keep a fixed slight bend in the arms.
2. Pull the shoulder blades together at the end of each rep.
3. Keep the torso upright and avoid using momentum.
4. Use a light load to keep tension on the rear delts.
